intent: A habit quiz that beats the British stereotype: bars put the three biggest tea drinkers to scale, a pin lands on the wet Black Sea hills where almost all of it is grown, and a teapot rides the road west across the country to the glasses where it ends up — grown at home, drunk all day.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Who drinks the MOST tea per person?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Who drinks the most tea per person?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Turkey. Over 3 kilos of tea per person a year, more than anyone on Earth.

lines.direction: ease back over Anatolia; three bars rise on 'Britain' with Turkey on top as the British flag-ball thinks; a dragon sticker on 'China' as Turkey pulses
lines.text: Britain is famous for it, yet comes third. China grew the leaf first, but drinks far less per head.

lines.direction: tighten on the eastern Black Sea; the grown-at-home tag on 'grown' with a leaf sticker; the Rize pin on 'hills'; a rain sticker on 'coast' as Turkey pulses
lines.text: Almost all of it is grown at home, on steep wet hills along the Black Sea coast.

lines.direction: pull back west along the coast; the tea road draws from the hills toward the Bosporus on 'travels' with a teapot riding it; the Istanbul pin and the BLACK TEA card on 'glasses'; a glass sticker on 'day' as the Turkish flag-ball grins and Turkey pulses; the pins leave at the end
lines.text: From there it travels across the country to tulip-shaped glasses, poured dozens of times a day.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A nation in a tea glass. Follow us.
